instruction: Add a title 'Paper Reading Notes - March 2024' at the very beginning of the opened document, before any existing content.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(1)

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent tried to access huggingface.co to find daily papers but encountered ERR_TIMED_OUT and certificate errors. After bypassing certificate warning, was redirected to unrelated JEIFM radio station. Spent all 47 turns retrying and attempting alternative approaches (curl, different URLs) but never accessed Huggingface or modified the docx.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome, type URLs in address bar, reload pages, interact with certificate warnings, use terminal for curl commands, switch between Chrome and LibreOffice Writer
metadata.failure_analysis: Huggingface.co was inaccessible in the VM environment due to network/proxy issues. The model never reached the point of editing the document because it was stuck on the web navigation part.
metadata.task_rationale: Focuses purely on the document editing aspect which the model demonstrated ability to interact with (LibreOffice Writer was open and visible). Removes the web dependency entirely.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding a header title at the beginning of the opened docx file. Custom getter reads the first paragraph of the saved docx. Custom metric checks if it matches the expected header text (case-insensitive). Partial credit (0.5) if the header appears anywhere in the document.

scoring_breakdown.header_at_top: 1.0 - Header text found as first paragraph
scoring_breakdown.header_anywhere: 0.5 - Header text found elsewhere in document

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly downloads and parses the docx file, extracting the first non-empty paragraph and all paragraphs - appropriate for verifying title placement at document beginning.
Metric correctly accesses expected.get('expected_header') directly from the rules dict, properly handling the type='rule' parameter convention.
Case-insensitive comparison is appropriate since the instruction specifies exact title text but casing may vary in user input.
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
Partial credit logic (1.0 for first paragraph, 0.5 for anywhere) is well-designed for this single-requirement task.

Minor: uses 'in' operator rather than equality for first paragraph check, which is slightly permissive (would pass if title is a substring of a longer first paragraph), but this is a reasonable approach.
